newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Clabecq to offer majority re-employment.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Clabecq to offer majority re-employment.

text.p: Belgium's Walloon regional government said on Thursday it hoped workers at bankrupt steel firm Clabecq would accept a proposal by receivers to re-employ about 1,400 of the 1,800-strong workforce.

"The (Walloon) government hopes that at their general assembly called for Friday the personnel go along with the receivers' proposals which allow for close to 1,400 workers to be taken on again immediately," it said in a statement.
Belgian radio said most of the remainder would be given early retirement. But the future of about 50 workers was still uncertain.
Socialist trade unionists, some of whom were meeting the receivers on Thursday, have said they opposed all redundancies.

The Walloon region said the move was necessary for activity to continue at the firm, and reiterated that Clabecq's long-term survival depended on a total or partial takeover by an industrial operator.

Through its SWS steel investment arm the region is Clabecq's majority shareholder, and has offered to meet future operating losses at the firm of up to 150 million Belgian francs for at least three months.
A Belgian court declared loss-making Clabecq bankrupt on January 3 and appointed four receivers to run the company which has a full order book for at least this quarter.
All workers are due to be laid off imminently, and court- appointed experts had initially proposed that just over 1,300 be immediately re-employed on short-term renewable contracts.
Saddled with high costs, poor margins and low-quality products, the company had been struggling to survive in a cyclical industry marked by overcapacity and cheap imports from eastern Europe.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy in mid-December after the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc ($47 million) rescue plan by the Walloon Region, which then withdrew its support from the firm.
The company's shares were delisted this week from the Brussels bourse where they had been quoted on the cash market.
